proposals.impact: converts 4 stalled intro-loads into quiz starts
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, four sessions reached quiz intro_load and zero progressed further. Start rate is 0%. Every visitor who found the quiz — two from a Google Apps Viewer URL (suggesting a shared doc or proposal), one from Bing, one direct — saw the intro and left. The drop is on the intro screen itself, not a later step.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is doing something that stops people before they commit a single click. The most common culprit is a vague value proposition that asks for trust the page has not yet earned. Rewrite the intro's headline and sub-copy to state a specific, grounded outcome in concrete language — what the person will know about themselves in the next four minutes — rather than category-level coaching language. Do not add a button; change the words above the existing one. Ground the copy in the £150k story or the gym-bag moment so it reads as lived, not templated.
proposals.current_text: Discover your money personality and unlock the insights you need to finally take control of your finances.
proposals.new_text:
Four minutes. Five questions. You'll leave knowing the one money pattern that explains most of the decisions you've been second-guessing.

Joel built this after noticing that his own £150k in earnings one year still left him staring at an unopened tax-return tab in October. The category wasn't the problem. The pattern underneath it was.

proposals.impact: lifts 37.5% open rate closer to Money Vigilance's 66.67% benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% across 16 sends, the lowest of the three active sequences. Money Vigilance is opening at 66.67% and Money Avoidance at 52.63%. The gap between Worship and Vigilance is 29 percentage points. Subject line quality is the highest-leverage single-file fix available for an automation.
proposals.proposal: The Money Worship subject line is almost certainly carrying category language ("money worship", "relationship with money", "your beliefs") that feels abstract to a reader who just found out their result. Replace it with a subject line that names the specific cost of the Money Worship pattern in a way only someone living it would recognise. Use the Sultanic test: could 1,000 coaches write this line? If yes, rewrite until no. No em dashes. No binary contrast structure. No adverb-led opener.
proposals.current_text: Your Money Worship result: here's what it means for you
proposals.new_text: You earned more this year and felt worse about money, not better. Here's why that's the pattern, not a personal failing.

proposals.impact: unblocks automated content pipeline stalled since 08:03 UTC
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 08:03 UTC and the Funnel-Hack Digest failed at 13:00 UTC on 11 September. The content queue shows only one post queued against 47 published. If the blog workflow stays broken, that queue post will not ship and the pipeline will stall entirely. All three commits in the last 24 hours are cursor-state chores, meaning no human has touched the workflow file to investigate the failure.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow YAML and check the failure. Common causes in Astro + GitHub Actions pipelines: an API key secret that has rotated or expired, a changed output path that the publish step can no longer find, or a Node version mismatch after a dependabot bump to package.json (which is blocked from Fred edits, but a human can check). Add a explicit echo of the relevant secret name (not its value) and the build output path into the workflow's pre-publish step so future failures surface the cause in the Actions log rather than silently exiting. This is a one-block addition to the existing jobs.publish.steps section.
proposals.current_text:
- name: Publish post
        run: node scripts/publish-post.js
proposals.new_text:
- name: Publish post
        run: |
          echo "Checking build output path before publish..."
          ls -la dist/content/blog/ || echo "WARNING: dist/content/blog/ not found — build may have failed silently"
          echo "Secret present check: MAILERLITE_API_KEY is ${{ secrets.MAILERLITE_API_KEY != '' && 'set' || 'MISSING' }}"
          node scripts/publish-post.js
